headline: UW-La Crosse separates from the WIAC
dek: UW-La Crosse finished with 24 wins and two losses without a draw across all matches, separating itself from the rest of the WIAC table. No other program in the conference stayed close before WashU ended its season.

pattern.label: derived
pattern.text: Attacking output in the WIAC splits sharply between the top and the field: UW-La Crosse's 92 goals outpace UW-Platteville, UW-Stevens Point, and UW-Stout combined, while the lower half of the conference clusters tightly together.

wire.line: UW-Whitewater conceded just nine goals all season while scoring 54 across all matches.

findings.label: observed
findings.text: UW-La Crosse forward Aubree Caya leads the conference's published scoring leaders with fifteen goals and six assists on 83 shots.

findings.label: observed
findings.text: UW-Eau Claire goalkeeper Bella Jones made 106 saves while allowing nineteen goals, posting a 0.848 save percentage.

findings.label: derived
findings.text: UW-Whitewater spread its attack across at least nineteen distinct goal scorers during the season.

findings.label: observed
findings.text: All three WIAC matches past their scheduled date with no published result belong to UW-Eau Claire, against Nazareth, Oswego State, and Buffalo State.

last_match.line: The loss snapped UW-La Crosse's winning run and brought the WIAC season to a close.

validation.policy: observed and derived claims are recomputed against the data home before publish; failures are dropped, not softened. signal and projected pass on schema unless the data contradicts a figure. context is never validated as a finding.
